CRIMINAL CASE No. 49740 of 2024  BRIJESH SILAWAT  Versus  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH  Appearance:
 Shri Palash Choudhary, learned counsel for the applic  Shri R.S.Suryavanshi, learned Govt.Advocate for the r  ORDER

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT INDORE
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is second application filed under Section 483 of the BNSS, 2023 for grant of bail to the applicant, in connection with FIR/Crime No.572/2023 dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station - Bhanwarkuan, Indore, District - Indore (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 of IPC.

2. Prosecution story, in brief is that house no.51, Manish Bagh Colony, Indore was owned by Ratanbai Silawat, who was wife of Lakshmi Narayan and mother of Vijay Silawat, Rajesh Silawat,
Raj Kumar, Manoj, Preeti Silawat, present applicant Brijesh and complainant Ramakant Silawat.

Smt. Ratanbai died on 13.09.2009 and thereafter, on 15.09.2023, husband of the deceased Lakshmi Narayan filed an application for mutation of his name in concerning record at place of Ratanbai before revenue officer, Nagar Nigam, Indore stating that other legal heirs have no objection if the name of applicant Lakshmi Narayan be mutated in the concerning record.

An affidavit was also filed by other legal heirs NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35232 2 MCRC-49740-2024 of the deceased with effect that they have no objection if name of applicant Lakshmi Narayan be mutated in the records.
On the basis of aforesaid, solely the name of co-accused Lakshmi Narayan was mutated in the place of Ratanbai in the record in year 2013.

It is alleged against the applicant Brijesh Silawat vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131687006/
1 and co-accused that the complainant Ramakant had neither given his consent to mutate the house only in the name of accused Lakshmi Naryan nor executed any affidavit in favour of co- accused Lakshmi Narayn.

sentences.text: It is also alleged that the present applicant and co- accused person had purchased a stamp paper in the name of complainant on 15.04.2013 and they have also put a forged signature of the applicant on the questioned affidavit.
Thereafter, both the present applicant and accused persons had taken loan of Rs.70,00,000/- from Chola Mandlam Finance Bank by mortgaging the aforesaid house.
At present loan amount with interest has become Rs.80,49,306/-.
There is irregularity in payment.
By this the accused persons have in order to take the land of share of the complainant and prepared forged document for the same and took a big loan.
As per report of handwriting expert signature of the complainant did not match with the signature of questioned affidavit.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant has not committed the offence and has falsely been implicated in the case.
It is submitted that the dispute is related between the applicant and his family members.

After dismissal of first application of the applicant, he deposited entire loan amount before the Chola Mandalam, which is Investment and Finance Company and the applicant has already filed NOC in the case issued by concerning Finance Company.
It is submitted that applicant is in custody since 1.6.2024.
After completion of investigation, charge sheet has been filed.
No custodial interrogation is required.
Conclusion of the trial will take sufficient long time for NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35232 3 MCRC-49740-2024 its disposal.
Under these circumstances, prayer is made for grant of bail to the applicant.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the non-applicant/State has opposed the prayer of the applicant and prayed for rejection of the application.
However, it is fairly submitted that applicant has deposited entire loan amount int he concerning Finance Company.

5. Having considered the submissions advanced from counsel for the parties, also considering the facts and circumstances, without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
Hence, the application is allowed.

6. It is directed that the applicant-Brijesh Silawat be released on bail upon his/her furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for his/her appearance before the trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the trial Court during pendency of the trial.
It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of section 480 (3) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
7. M.Cr.C. stands disposed of, accordingly.
C.c. as per rules.

(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE patil Brijesh Silawat vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131687006/
